items.q: What is a "freedom figure" and how do you calculate it?
items.a: Your freedom figure is the invested amount that generates enough **passive income to live without working**. Set a lifestyle baseline by category, then apply the **rule of 25** (≈4% safe withdrawal). Gen Z aspirational example: ~$75,325/year → ×25 = **$1,883,125**.

items.q: How should you treat that invested pile once you have it?
items.a: Like a **golden goose**: take the eggs each year, don't eat the goose. Primary vehicle: **S&P 500 index fund** via dollar-cost averaging; past 10-year returns ~12–14% are not a guarantee.

items.q: Which expense hacks compound the most?
items.a: **Car hacking**: buy quality used at depreciation bottom; avoid the **$734/mo** average new-car payment (~$9K/year). **Brand hacking**: Cocoa Pops $4.25 vs Choco Rice $1.66 — one cereal swap can save ~**$934/year** ($2.56/day).

items.q: What are house, tax, and deal hacking?
items.a: **House hacking**: duplex rent covers mortgage, or Airbnb a premium unit part-time. **Tax hacking**: legal deductions + ISA £20K / Roth IRA. **Deal hacking**: never pay sticker; use CarMax/Carvana quotes as a ceiling; time purchases end-of-month.

items.q: Why get a credit card if debt is scary?
items.a: Used wisely (**low balance, pay in full monthly**), cards build the credit score that unlocks **lower mortgage rates**. Ignored score → sky-high rates or rejection at 28. Credit is a tool, not a trap, when disciplined.

items.q: How do you answer "I'm too busy for a side hustle"?
items.a: Income stool: one job = one leg. Math: 168 hr/week − 40 work − 56 sleep − 20.5 meals/commute = **50+ free hours**. Pick hustles that leverage **existing skills** (affiliate, freelance, e-commerce, cleaning).

items.q: How do rich people use money differently?
items.a: **Money-as-expansion**: poor pay bills; middle build credit for bigger loans/status; rich use money to **make more money**. Don't lifestyle-creep when income rises — reinvest instead of flex.

items.q: What passive stack does Tilbury recommend?
items.a: **S&P 500 primary**, crypto ~**5%** (Bitcoin/Ethereum, prepared to lose), plus real estate via house hacking or rentals. Mark's path: maxed hours flipping cars → realized he needed money that grows **while sleeping**.
